During the inspection, multiple locations were flagged on-site by their own crew, and the camera was unable to pass through the entire line, indicating additional blockages or potential collapses. This was also consistent with prior cabling and snaking attempts from other technicians.
However, the final report only documented a single failure point near the vent and recommended a limited 5–10 ft repair — which does not reflect the actual condition of the line.
When we questioned this, we were told that additional issues would require extra payment to be included in the report, even though:
The issues were already observed during the same visit
Their own crew marked multiple problem areas
Prior service reports confirmed similar obstructions
This puts property owners in a very difficult position, especially when dealing with city approvals or sewer lateral programs that rely strictly on the written report.
It raises serious concerns when field findings are not fully documented unless additional fees are paid.
We strongly recommend that anyone using this company:
Request full documentation of all observed issues
Be present during inspection
Confirm what will and will not be included in the report before work begins
Very disappointing experience.

name: Rachel Hart
quote:
The Sewer Pros came to the house during our inspection period while in escrow while in the process of purchasing a new home. They did a sewer scope and provided their report stating the pipes were in good condition although they are old and had a lot of build up, and recommended a hydro jetting. Based on Sewer Pros report we felt comfortable that the pipes were in good condition and that positively impacted our decision to buy the house. A few weeks later right before moving in, we noticed the toilets slow draining and water coming up instead of down, then I decided to hired a plumber to come over to look at this issue. This company said there was a clog ran another camera inspection in the sewer to only find out the pipes were in terrible and deteriorating condition in multiple areas. After comparing both videos, this plumber realized Sewer Pros missed out on scoping multiple areas during their inspection. When I reached out to Sewer Pros and explained what was going on, they asked to come back and re-inspect. This time their manager was the one who came. Josh did his inspection this time using the clean outs in the front yard and decided their first assessment was accurate. Sewer Pros took ZERO accountability for a major miss on their part. Two weeks later after Josh performed the re-inspection, we came to find some water puddling up in the front yard by the clean outs. Thinking it was an irrigation issue, my husband went to check it out to only find out the clean out caps were un-screwed. When Josh came to re-inspect he left the clean outs OPEN!!! This caused sewage water to puddle up on my front lawn as well as mulch and dirt to go into the drains. This caused another clog in the pipes and during the labor day weekend we had to call an emergency plumbing service to come over.
When reaching out to Sewer Pros Friday before labor day, no one would answer the phone later on Friday or Saturday morning and all we got was a unprofessional answer from Josh via email. The emergency plumber also mentioned the pipe that run to the street was collapsed. After so many validations regarding issues with the pipes we decided to have a few other companies come by to evaluate these pipes issues and how much would cost to fix it. By the way, all the companies that have come here and done an inspection recommended AGAINST hydro jetting due to the state of the pipes, this was exactly what Sewer Pros recommended, which the high pressure would have likely busted the pipes. The issues I've had to fix due to Sewer Pros negligence and incompetence are now in the $30K.
We never got one message or call apologizing or being empathetic for their mistakes, quite the contrary. Their business model is very well thought, "we ONLY do inspections (and hydro jetting) hence we are unbiased and don't try to push any work on our clients", the truth is, their are just checking the boxes. When you hire them for the only thing they do, sewer scope, they rush the cam down the pipes, provide you the video and that's it. They actually don't even have a plumbing license so that's why they can't do any work themselves!
I recommend you have your pipes inspected by California Plumbing, Drain Mob, Almco Plumbing or Core Plumbing instead who are professional and ethical businesses. Stay away from The Sewer Pros at all costs!

I met the plumber from the other company at our former home and told him of the report we received from Sewer Pros.    He then took the cap off the stack and asked me what I heard.  I told him it sounded like water and he said it was the water main and if it was blocked we would not be hearing water.  Based on this, he decided not to cable but instead to try running the camera through which he did without any issues stating on our paid receipt "Had no problem running camera through.  Sewer in good condition".    Also in the inspection video he stated the following:  "small amount of buildup right off the bat, did not encounter any other issue what so ever".

I contacted Sewer Pros to let them know how extremely unhappy my husband and we were.  They stated they did nothing wrong, they stand by their recommendation and that they were unable to get their camera through and there is still a heavy amount of buildup in the line & their recommendation was and still is that it should be cabled out.

This is totally riduculous.  The facts speak for themselves.  Sewer Pros is stating the buildup was so bad they could not get their camera through.  Another plumbing company can pass a camera through with absolutely no issues!
Sewer Pros sees 'heavy buildup" that is so bad it prevents them from getting their camera thru and another plumbing company can easily get their camera through with no issues & without the line being cabled out.

I normally do not post bad reviews however this was so bad and upsetting that I had to warn other people.  I hope other people read this review and do not use Sewer Pros.

I called another plumbing company to come out and take a look.  The technician from the second plumbing company cut the drywall in the ceiling below the tub and we could see the hole that was put into the drain pipe from the cable.  Once the new technician replaced the broken pipe, he also snaked the drain because it was still draining slow.  He did it manually with a cable, not a machine, and said this is the preferred way as it's less likely to cause damage to the pipes.

I also had a contractor come out and take out all the drywall in the bathroom as the water ran across the ceiling and down the walls.

I sent the photos that are attached to the company, along with the bill for the second plumber and the contractor and they told me that they are not responsible for repairs and wouldn't pay them.  I spoke with Kathy on the phone and again was told they were not going to pay for the damage caused by their technician.  I asked for the owner's name and number and she refused to give it to me.

This tub and the pipe in question were installed when the bathroom was updated several years ago and were not old or corroded or damaged in any way as is clearly shown in the photos. There was never a pipe leak before they came.  It's been almost a month and my bathroom is still down to the studs so I will have to go through the process of getting new drywall installed and painted with all the resulting dust and inconvenience and cost.

This company made a mistake, it happens, but their refusal to take responsibility for it is ridiculous.
